result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as test code (mock resources), whatever the rest of the name is. The new test passes.

- **Change:** in `codeanalyzer/.../scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, the two rules `.*/__mock…/.*` and `.*/mock…/.*` now use `[^/\\]*` for the rest of the folder name instead of `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`. That covers plain `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`.
- **Scope of the match:** it stops at the first `/` or `\`, so it stays within one folder name. `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are not matched.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already normalizes backslashes, so no change was needed there.
- **Test:** I added `MockFolderConventionTest` in `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/`. It checks that all the old folder names (`mocks`, `__mocks__`, `mock-data`, `mock_data`, `mock data`, `mockStore`) and the new ones match, with both `/` and `\` separators. It also checks that the non-mock paths don't match.

I did not run the rest of the `codeanalyzer` tests, and nothing is committed.
